browserhive/axtree-shape.collapsed-role: line {line}: roles that should have been collapsed are still in the tree ({roles})
browserhive/axtree-shape.desc: browserhive: checks the recorded accessibility tree against the pruning rules the profile declares
browserhive/axtree-shape.not-json: {entry} line {line} is not a JSON object
browserhive/axtree-shape.unknown-propert: line {line}: nodes carry properties this profile does not allow ({keys})
browserhive/behaviors-shape.desc: browserhive: checks the contents of behaviors/custom.jsonl against settings.behaviors. Every behavior the settings report as coming from the request must have its source here — that source arrived with the request and is recoverable from nowhere else once the response is discarded. The converse is not required: a line may have no matching entry, because a behavior can be placed in the page and then decline to act, and the code still ran.
browserhive/behaviors-shape.missing-entr: settings.behaviors reports {id} as request-supplied, but behaviors/custom.jsonl is absent
browserhive/behaviors-shape.missing-memb: behaviors/custom.jsonl line {line} is missing {members} (required by profile 1.5.0)
browserhive/behaviors-shape.not-json: behaviors/custom.jsonl line {line} is not a JSON object
browserhive/behaviors-shape.source-missi: settings.behaviors reports {id} as request-supplied, but behaviors/custom.jsonl has no line for it
browserhive/behaviors-shape.unknown-prof: behaviors/custom.jsonl line {line} declares profile {found}, which this version does not define
browserhive/dismissal-shape.desc: browserhive: checks the shape of browserhive:capture.dismissal when it is present. It must carry the selectors and heuristic that were in force even when nothing was removed — an empty list of removals reads the same whether twenty selectors were tried or none, so the outcome is only checkable next to the input. And a removal that could not be carried out must state that instead of reporting an empty result, because it observed nothing.
browserhive/dismissal-shape.missing-memb: dismissal is missing {member} (required by profile 1.4.0 whenever dismissal is present)
browserhive/dismissal-shape.not-object: browserhive:capture.dismissal is {found}, expected a JSON object
browserhive/dismissal-shape.unreadable-w: dismissal carries unreadable alongside {members} — a removal that could not be carried out has observed nothing, so it must not also state a result
browserhive/dismissal-shape.wrong-type: dismissal.{member} is {found}, which is not the type profile 1.4.0 defines
browserhive/settings-shape.desc: browserhive: checks that browserhive:capture.settings carries every member profile 1.3.0 requires. Without this check a producer can drop a required member and still claim conformance — which is how the cache member stayed in 1.1.0 for several releases after no implementation wrote it.
browserhive/settings-shape.wrong-type: settings.{member} is {found}, which is not the type profile 1.3.0 defines
browserhive/settle-deadline.desc: browserhive: reports an archive whose wait after navigation ran into its deadline, naming the signals that were not satisfied. This is not a violation — profile 1.7.0 says a deadline is not a failure, and the package holds what the page had become by then. It is shown because a reader weighing the archive as evidence needs to know the page was still changing when it was taken, and nothing else in the archive says so.
browserhive/settle-deadline.still-changi: the page had not settled when it was captured: {signals} not satisfied by the deadline (waited {waitedMs} ms of {maxMs} ms)
browserhive/settle-shape.deadline-withou: settle.endedBy is "deadline" but every signal has a time — a wait that met every signal ended quiet
browserhive/settle-shape.desc: browserhive: checks browserhive:capture.settle against profile 1.7.0. It must be present, since the wait runs on every capture. Every signal's time must be written, as null when the signal was not satisfied: an omitted time reads as a signal nobody watched. And endedBy must agree with the times — "quiet" beside a null, or "deadline" with none, is a claim the capture did not earn.
browserhive/settle-shape.missing-time: settle.{member} is absent — a signal that was not satisfied is written as null, and an absent time reads as a signal that was not watched
browserhive/settle-shape.not-object: browserhive:capture.settle is {found}, expected a JSON object
browserhive/settle-shape.quiet-with-null: settle.endedBy is "quiet" but {signals} not satisfied — a wait that missed a signal ended on its deadline
browserhive/settle-shape.wrong-type: settle.{member} is {found}, which is not the type profile 1.7.0 defines
browserhive/storage-inventory.desc: browserhive: checks that the archive records what web storage the captured origins held. The inventory is required by profile 1.1.0: without it a reader cannot tell a page that rendered from localStorage from one that had nothing to show, and completeness cannot say so because storage never became a body.
browserhive/storage-inventory.digest-sha: {where}.digest is {found}, expected sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hex digits
browserhive/storage-inventory.origin-for: {where} must carry either both areas or unreadable: true — an origin that was empty and one that could not be read are different claims
browserhive/storage-inventory.oversize-s: {where}.valuesOversize is {found}, expected true — the member has one meaning and says it by being present
browserhive/storage-inventory.oversize-w: {where} carries both valuesOversize and unreadable — storage that could not be read has no size to have exceeded
{where} carries valuesOversize but storage.valuesRecorded is not true — no origin's values were going to be carried, so nothing was dropped at a bound
browserhive/storage-shape.areas-shape: line {line}: areas must contain local and session, each a JSON object
browserhive/storage-shape.declared-but-a: storage.valuesRecorded is true but {entry} is not in the package
browserhive/storage-shape.desc: browserhive: checks storage/origins.jsonl against the profile, and against what the inventory says about it. A reader decides whether the archive carries stored values by reading valuesRecorded alone, so the two must agree.
browserhive/storage-shape.not-json: {entry} line {line} is not a JSON object
browserhive/storage-shape.oversize-has-v: line {line}: {origin} is recorded as valuesOversize in the inventory but has values here — the inventory says they were too large to carry, and here they are
browserhive/storage-shape.present-but-un: {entry} is present but storage.valuesRecorded is not true
browserhive/storage-shape.unreadable-has: line {line}: {origin} is recorded as unreadable in the inventory but has values here
browserhive/tls-chain.bad-signature: {host}: certificate {index} is linked to the next one but its signature does not verify
browserhive/tls-chain.broken-link: {host}: certificate {index} does not link to the next one (issuer {issuer} vs subject {nextSubject})
browserhive/tls-chain.dangling-ref: {host}: chainRef {chainRef} points at no entry in tls.chains
browserhive/tls-chain.desc: browserhive: verifies the certificate chains in tls, using only what the package itself holds
browserhive/tls-chain.leaf-not-first: {host}: the first certificate does not cover this host (subject {subject}) — the leaf is not first
browserhive/tls-chain.unparseable: {host}: the chain behind {chainRef} could not be parsed as certificates
browserhive/tls-chain.verified: verified the certificate chain of {hosts} host(s)
browserhive/tls-san.desc: browserhive: checks the recorded san against the certificate the package carries
browserhive/tls-san.drift: {host}: san records {recorded} name(s) but the certificate carries {certificate}
browserhive/tls-san.host-not-covered: {host}: none of the recorded san names covers this host ({san})
browserhive/tls-san.missing: {host}: san is missing or is not an array of names
browserhive/url-policies.absent: settings.urlPolicies is missing. Profile 1.3.0 requires it even when no request matched: an empty array is the claim that no policy was in force
browserhive/url-policies.bad-pattern: settings.urlPolicies has {count} entries whose pattern is not a string. A record of a withheld request names the pattern that matched, and a reader looks it up here
browserhive/url-policies.desc: browserhive: checks that the archive declares, in order, what the capture did about each URL pattern in force. Profile 1.3.0 requires the list even when nothing matched, because an empty list is the claim that nothing was filtered; and it requires an action on each entry, because that is what says whether the request was sent at all.
browserhive/url-policies.not-array: settings.urlPolicies is {found}, expected an array of objects
browserhive/url-policies.unknown-action: settings.urlPolicies uses actions this version does not define: {found}. The action is what says whether the request was sent (deny) or sent but not kept (no-archive)
browserhive/policy-not-truncated.desc: browserhive: a body a policy omitted must not be listed as dropped at a size limit (completeness.truncatedUrls)
browserhive/policy-not-truncated.url-pol: {url} is listed in completeness.truncatedUrls, but the URL policy {pattern} (no-body) omitted its body — a body the capture never fetched cannot have reached a size limit
browserhive/policy-not-truncated.content: {url} is listed in completeness.truncatedUrls, but the content-type policy {prefix} omitted its body — a body the capture never fetched cannot have reached a size limit
browserhive/document-withheld.desc: browserhive: the page's text, its title and its accessibility tree are read from the rendered page, so a policy that kept the document's body out of the archive does not by itself keep them out. Checks browserhive:capture.document against profile 1.11.0 (an archive that conforms to 1.10.0 is held to 1.10.0, where deny withholds nothing): withheld must be what the policies give for the document it names, in both directions; a withheld document leaves no text or title on its page entry and no accessibility tree; otherwise the tree names that document, not the requested URL
browserhive/document-withheld.not-object: browserhive:capture.document is {found}, expected a JSON object
browserhive/document-withheld.missing-ur: document has no url; only an unattributed document may leave it out
browserhive/document-withheld.unknown-re: document.withheld is {found}, which the profile the archive conforms to does not define (url-policy, content-type, no-archive, unattributed, and from 1.11.0 deny)
browserhive/document-withheld.should-wit: the policies give {expected} for the document {url}, but document.withheld is absent — its text, title and tree stayed in the archive although the policy kept its body out
browserhive/document-withheld.should-not: document.withheld is {declared}, but no policy applies to the document {url} — a policy that matched only a redirect hop or a document the page left withholds nothing
browserhive/document-withheld.wrong-reas: document.withheld is {declared}, but the policies give {expected} for the document {url}
browserhive/document-withheld.text-prese: the page entry has text although document.withheld is {withheld}
browserhive/document-withheld.title-pres: the page entry has a title although document.withheld is {withheld}
browserhive/document-withheld.axtree-pre: accessibility/axtree.jsonl is present although document.withheld is {withheld} — the tree carries the page's text
browserhive/document-withheld.text-withh: the page entry's textWithheld is {textWithheld}, but document.withheld is {withheld}
the page entry's textWithheld is {textWithheld}, but document.withheld is absent
browserhive/document-withheld.tree-url: line {line} of the accessibility tree names {treeUrl}, but the document it was read from is {url}
browserhive/document-withheld.not-in-arc: the document {url} is neither in the index nor in a no-archive record (from profile 1.11.0, nor a deny record) — the archive holds no record of the document the page was read from
browserhive/deny-enforced.desc: browserhive: a deny policy promises that the request is never sent. Checks the WARC for request, response or revisit records of URLs whose first matching urlPolicies entry is deny; only a metadata record saying the request was withheld may stand for such a URL (profile 1.11.0)
browserhive/deny-enforced.sent: {url} has a {type} record although the first policy to match it, {pattern}, is deny — the request left the capturing machine
browserhive/window-shape.desc: browserhive: a record of a window not opened (a metadata record carrying window) says window: not-opened, names in WARC-Target-URI the URL the window would have loaded, names page or iframe in target when it has one, and carries no action — it is not a record of a withheld request (profile 1.12.0)
browserhive/window-shape.value: {url}: window is {value}, but this profile defines only not-opened
browserhive/window-shape.uri: a window record (window: {value}) has no WARC-Target-URI — the URL the window would have loaded is what the record is for
browserhive/window-shape.target: {url}: target is {target}, but a window is asked for by a page or an iframe
browserhive/window-shape.action: {url}: a window record carries action {action} — it is not a record of a withheld request
browserhive/unintercepted-listed.desc: browserhive: bodies that crossed the wire but could not be read as bytes (metadata truncated: not-intercepted) are listed in completeness.uninterceptedUrls, and their response records carry WARC-Truncated: unspecified (profile 1.13.0)
browserhive/unintercepted-listed.unliste: {url} has a record of a body not intercepted (truncated: not-intercepted) but is missing from completeness.uninterceptedUrls — the archive does not declare the missing body
browserhive/unintercepted-listed.unrecor: {url} is listed in completeness.uninterceptedUrls, but no record says truncated: not-intercepted for it
browserhive/unintercepted-listed.truncat: {url}: the response of a body not intercepted has WARC-Truncated {value}; it must be unspecified, or a reader of the WARC alone takes the empty payload for the body
browserhive/payload-charset.desc: browserhive: a text body that looks re-encoded by the writer rather than kept as the bytes the server sent (profile 1.13.0 forbids converting a body's character encoding; a guess, so a warning)
browserhive/payload-charset.transcoded: {url}: Content-Type declares charset={charset}, but the body does not decode as {charset} and does decode as UTF-8 — it looks rewritten to UTF-8
browserhive/payload-charset.double-encod: {url}: read as UTF-8 and turned back into windows-1252 bytes, the body decodes as UTF-8 again — it looks like a UTF-8 body read as windows-1252 and written back as UTF-8
browserhive/warc-files.desc: browserhive: archive/ holds only data-NNN.warc.gz, numbered contiguously from 000; each file begins with a warcinfo that names it; every file but the last is at least settings.limits.maxWarcBytes long (profile 1.14.0)
browserhive/warc-files.name: {entry} is not named data-NNN.warc.gz — the archive directory holds only files of that name
browserhive/warc-files.gap: the WARC files are not numbered contiguously: expected {expected}, found {found}
browserhive/warc-files.first-record: {entry} does not begin with a warcinfo record (first record: {type})
browserhive/warc-files.filename: {entry}: its warcinfo names {found}; WARC-Filename must be the file's own name
browserhive/warc-files.under-limit: {entry} is {size} bytes, under maxWarcBytes {limit}, yet it is not the last file — a new file starts only once the current one reaches the limit
browserhive/warc-files.max-warc-bytes: settings.limits.maxWarcBytes is {found}; it must be a positive integer (bytes)
browserhive/exchange-in-one-file.desc: browserhive: the response, request and metadata records of one exchange are in the same WARC file (profile 1.14.0)
browserhive/exchange-in-one-file.request: {url}: a record in {entry} is concurrent to a record in {other} — one exchange must not span files
browserhive/exchange-in-one-file.metadat: {url}: a metadata record in {entry} refers to a record in {other} — one exchange must not span files
browserhive/warcinfo-declares-profile.de: browserhive: each WARC file's warcinfo declares, in exactly one conformsTo field, the version of BrowserHive WARC Profile the file conforms to, and every file of the archive declares the same one (profile 1.16.0)
browserhive/warcinfo-declares-profile.mi: {entry}: its warcinfo has no conformsTo — from profile 1.16.0, each WARC file names the BrowserHive WARC Profile version it conforms to
browserhive/warcinfo-declares-profile.re: {entry}: its warcinfo has {count} conformsTo fields ({found}); it must have exactly one
browserhive/warcinfo-declares-profile.va: {entry}: its warcinfo conformsTo is {found}, which is not the URL of a BrowserHive WARC Profile version (https://uraitakahito.github.io/browserhive-warc-spec/N.N.N/)
browserhive/warcinfo-declares-profile.mi: {entry}: its warcinfo declares {found}, but {first} declares {expected} — every WARC file of one archive declares the same version
cdxj/filename-archive-relative.desc: indexes/index.cdxj entries must use archive-relative filenames (not "archive/...")
cdxj/filename-archive-relative.starts-wi: {entry} entry "filename" starts with "archive/" — wabac.js prepends archive/ itself, double-prefix breaks replay
cdxj/index-not-gzipped.desc: indexes/index.cdxj must not be gzipped (wabac.js silently ignores .cdxj.gz)
cdxj/index-not-gzipped.gzip-magic: {entry} starts with the gzip magic bytes — the file is named correctly but the content is compressed
cdxj/index-not-gzipped.gzipped-entry: Entry "{name}" is a gzipped CDXJ — wabac.js does not recognise .cdxj.gz / .cdx.gz
cdxj/index-recognised-by-wabac.desc: WACZ must contain a wabac-recognised index (.cdx / .cdxj / .idx)
cdxj/index-recognised-by-wabac.missing-p: {name} references "{pair}" but no such entry exists in the WACZ
cdxj/index-recognised-by-wabac.no-index: No wabac-recognised index file found under indexes/ — wabac.js needs at least one .cdx / .cdxj / .idx entry to serve any URL
cdxj/index-valid-data.desc: index CDXJ (plain or gzipped) must contain valid CDXJ data (WACZ §5.2.2)
cdxj/index-valid-data.gzip-error: {entry} is named as gzipped but could not be decompressed (WACZ §5.2.2: index files MUST contain CDXJ data)
cdxj/index-valid-data.invalid: {entry} line {line} is not valid CDXJ ({reason}) (WACZ §5.2.2: index files MUST contain CDXJ data)
cdxj/pages-mainpage.desc: datapackage.mainPageURL must appear in both pages/pages.jsonl and indexes/index.cdxj
cdxj/pages-mainpage.no-cdxj-record: datapackage.json mainPageURL "{url}" has no record in indexes/index.cdxj
cdxj/pages-mainpage.not-in-pages: datapackage.json mainPageURL "{url}" is not listed in pages/pages.jsonl
cdxj/warc-offsets.desc: indexes/index.cdxj offset/length must land on a WARC gzip-member boundary
cdxj/warc-offsets.length-mismatch: indexes/index.cdxj line {line}: length {length} does not match WARC member at offset {offset} (actual {actual})
cdxj/warc-offsets.missing-or-nonnumeric: indexes/index.cdxj line {line}: offset / length missing or not numeric
cdxj/warc-offsets.offset-no-match: indexes/index.cdxj line {line}: offset {offset} does not match any WARC gzip-member start
cdxj/warc-offsets.file-not-in-archive: indexes/index.cdxj line {line}: filename {filename} names no file under archive/
datapackage/digest.absent: datapackage-digest.json is absent (WACZ §5.2.5: SHOULD be included to verify datapackage.json)
datapackage/digest.desc: datapackage-digest.json should be present and its hash must match datapackage.json (WACZ §5.2.5)
datapackage/digest.hash-mismatch: {entry} hash does not match the actual datapackage.json sha256
datapackage/frictionless-schema.desc: datapackage.json should conform to the Frictionless v1 schema (auxiliary)
datapackage/frictionless-structure.desc: datapackage.json must declare a non-empty resources array; each resource needs name and path (or data)
datapackage/frictionless-structure.no-re: datapackage.json has no resources (a non-empty resources array is required)
datapackage/profile-required.invalid-jso: {entry} is not valid JSON or not an object
datapackage/resource-hashes.desc: datapackage.json resource hashes must match the WACZ contents
datapackage/resource-hashes.invalid-path: {entry} resource is missing or has an invalid "path"
datapackage/resource-hashes.no-resources: {entry} has no "resources" array (or it is empty)
datapackage/resource-hashes.resource-mis: Resource "{path}" listed in {entry} is missing from the WACZ
datapackage/resources-complete.desc: every file in the WACZ must be listed in datapackage.json resources (WACZ MUST)
datapackage/resources-complete.orphan: {entry} is not listed in datapackage.json resources (WACZ MUST list all additional files)
datapackage/wacz-version-required.desc: datapackage.json must declare a non-empty wacz_version
i18n.smoke: {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} missing
report.more: {message} (and {more, plural, one {1 more} other {# more}} like this in the same file)
pages/page-schema.desc: each pages/pages.jsonl page line must be valid JSON with url and ts (WACZ §5.2.3)
pages/page-schema.missing-prop: pages/pages.jsonl line {line} is missing required properties: {props}
pages/page-schema.not-json: pages/pages.jsonl line {line} is not valid JSON
wacz-auth/signature.cert-unparseable: signedData.domainCert is not a readable PEM certificate chain
wacz-auth/signature.desc: wacz-auth: checks that the signature in datapackage-digest.json covers the hash it claims, under the certificate the package carries, and that the certificate covers the domain it names. Uses only what the package holds — whether the chain reaches a trusted root, and whether the timestamp is valid, are the verifier's own decisions and are not asked here.
wacz-auth/signature.domain-mismatch: signedData.domainCert does not cover {domain} — the certificate that signed this archive is for a different name
wacz-auth/signature.signature-mismatch: signedData.signature does not verify against signedData.hash under the certificate in domainCert — the signature does not cover this archive
wacz-auth/signature.verified: signature verifies against the hash, under a certificate covering {domain} (chain trust and timestamp are not checked here)
wacz/required-files.desc: WACZ §5.2 requires these files/directories to exist
wacz/required-files.missing-archive: archive/ has no WARC file (WACZ §5.2.1: MUST contain at least one .warc/.warc.gz)
wacz/required-files.missing-datapackage: datapackage.json is missing (WACZ §5.2.4: MUST exist at the root)
wacz/required-files.missing-indexes: indexes/ has no index file (WACZ §5.2.2: MUST contain at least one .cdx/.cdxj/.idx)
wacz/required-files.missing-pages: pages/pages.jsonl is missing (WACZ §5.2.3: MUST be present)
wacz/reserved-dirs-clean.desc: no custom files may be added to the reserved archive/ indexes/ pages/ directories (WACZ MUST NOT)
wacz/reserved-dirs-clean.unexpected: {entry} is an unexpected file in the reserved "{dir}" directory (WACZ MUST NOT add custom files there)
warc/extension-gzip-match.desc: archive WARCs must use .warc.gz when GZIP-encoded and .warc otherwise (WACZ §5.2.1)
warc/extension-gzip-match.gz-needs-gz-ex: {entry} is GZIP-encoded but does not use the .warc.gz extension (WACZ §5.2.1: GZIP WARCs MUST use .warc.gz)
warc/extension-gzip-match.plain-has-gz-e: {entry} uses the .warc.gz extension but its content is not GZIP-encoded
warc/members-independent.decode-failed: Failed to decode gzip member at offset {offset} (length {length})
warc/members-independent.desc: every WARC under archive/ must concatenate independent gzip members
warc/members-independent.no-members: {entry} contains no gzip members (empty or unrecognised)
warc/record-structure.desc: Every WARC record has the shape WARC 1.1 gives a record: a WARC/1.1 version line, name: value fields that end in CRLF, a blank line, a block of Content-Length bytes and a closing CRLF CRLF
warc/record-structure.no-version-line: WARC record #{record} does not start with a WARC version line (found "{found}") — it is not read as a record
warc/record-structure.version-not-1-1: WARC record #{record} declares {found}, not WARC/1.1 — it is checked against the WARC 1.1 rules anyway
warc/record-structure.lf-line-ending: WARC record #{record}: header lines end in LF instead of CRLF
warc/record-structure.no-blank-line: WARC record #{record}: no blank line separates the header from the block — it is not read as a record
warc/record-structure.bad-field-line: WARC record #{record}, header line {line}: "{found}" is not a name: value field
warc/record-structure.folded-line: WARC record #{record}, header line {line}: the value of {found} is folded onto a continuation line
warc/record-structure.non-utf8: WARC record #{record}: the header is not valid UTF-8
warc/record-structure.content-length-mis: WARC record #{record} has no Content-Length, so the end of its block cannot be found
warc/record-structure.content-length-for: WARC record #{record}: Content-Length "{found}" is not a number of bytes
warc/record-structure.content-length-mis: WARC record #{record}: Content-Length says {declared} bytes but the block has {actual}
warc/record-structure.no-terminator: WARC record #{record}: the block is not followed by the CRLF CRLF that ends a record
warc/record-structure.first-record-not-w: the file starts with a {type} record — WARC 1.1 recommends starting each file with a warcinfo record
warc/mandatory-fields.desc: WARC records carry the fields WARC 1.1 makes mandatory: WARC-Record-ID, WARC-Date and WARC-Type on every record, and WARC-Target-URI, WARC-Profile and the segment fields where the record type needs them
warc/mandatory-fields.missing: WARC record #{record} has no {field}, which every record must have
warc/mandatory-fields.missing-for-type: WARC record #{record} ({type}) has no {field}, which a {type} record must have
warc/fields-by-type.desc: WARC records carry only the fields WARC 1.1 allows for their type, and no defined field twice (WARC-Concurrent-To excepted)
warc/fields-by-type.forbidden: WARC record #{record} ({type}) has {field}, which a {type} record must not carry
warc/fields-by-type.repeated: WARC record #{record} has {field} {count} times — it may appear only once
warc/fields-by-type.undefined-field: WARC record #{record} ({type}) has {field}, which WARC 1.1 does not define for {type} records
warc/field-values.desc: The values of the WARC 1.1 fields have the form the standard gives them: record IDs in angle brackets, bare URIs, W3CDTF timestamps in UTC, numbers, labelled digests, IP addresses and media types
warc/field-values.record-id-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not a URI in angle brackets
warc/field-values.uri-angle-brackets: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is wrapped in angle brackets, which WARC 1.1 dropped from this field
warc/field-values.uri-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not an absolute URI
warc/field-values.date-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not a W3CDTF timestamp
warc/field-values.date-fraction-digits: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" has more than 9 digits of fractional seconds
warc/field-values.date-not-utc: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not in UTC
warc/field-values.digits-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not a decimal number
warc/field-values.digest-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not of the form algorithm:value
warc/field-values.ip-brackets: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is wrapped in brackets — an IPv6 address is written bare
warc/field-values.ip-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is neither a dotted-quad IPv4 nor an IPv6 address
warc/field-values.media-type-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not a media type (type/subtype with optional parameters)
warc/field-values.digest-label-uppercase: WARC record #{record}: {field} uses the label "{label}" — labels are recommended in lowercase
warc/field-values.ip-not-canonical: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not in the canonical IPv6 form ({canonical})
warc/field-values.unknown-record-type: WARC record #{record} has the type "{value}", which WARC 1.1 does not define — readers ignore such records
warc/field-values.unknown-truncated-reas: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not one of length, time, disconnect and unspecified
warc/content-type.desc: WARC records carry the Content-Type WARC 1.1 recommends: one on every non-empty block, application/http on HTTP requests and responses, application/warc-fields on warcinfo
warc/content-type.missing: WARC record #{record} ({type}) has a block but no Content-Type
warc/content-type.not-application-http: WARC record #{record} ({type}) of an HTTP URI has Content-Type "{value}" instead of application/http
warc/content-type.msgtype-mismatch: WARC record #{record} ({type}) says msgtype={msgtype} in its Content-Type
warc/content-type.warcinfo-not-warc-fiel: WARC record #{record} (warcinfo) has Content-Type "{value}" — application/warc-fields is recommended
warc/revisit.desc: revisit records follow their WARC-Profile: one of the two WARC 1.1 profiles, a WARC-Payload-Digest and WARC-Truncated: length for identical-payload-digest, and the recommended WARC-Refers-To fields
warc/revisit.unknown-profile: WARC record #{record} (revisit) names the profile {value}, which WARC 1.1 does not define — readers do not interpret its block
warc/revisit.profile-uri-1-0: WARC record #{record} (revisit) is WARC/1.1 but names the WARC 1.0 profile {value}
warc/revisit.digest-missing: WARC record #{record} (revisit, identical-payload-digest) has no WARC-Payload-Digest
warc/revisit.truncated-missing: WARC record #{record} (revisit, identical-payload-digest) keeps a block but has no WARC-Truncated: length
warc/revisit.truncated-not-length: WARC record #{record} (revisit, identical-payload-digest) keeps a block with WARC-Truncated "{found}" — the reason must be length
warc/segmentation.desc: Segmented records form a proper series: an origin numbered 1, continuations numbered from 2 without gaps, one target URI, and a WARC-Segment-Total-Length on the last continuation that matches the blocks
warc/segmentation.origin-number: WARC record #{record} starts a segmented series but has WARC-Segment-Number {found}, not 1
warc/segmentation.origin-is-continuation: WARC record #{record} names {origin} as its origin, which is itself a continuation
warc/segmentation.number-sequence: WARC record #{record}: the continuations of this series are numbered {found} — they must count up from 2 by one
warc/segmentation.target-uri-differs: WARC record #{record} (continuation) has WARC-Target-URI {found}, but its series has {expected}
warc/segmentation.total-length-missing: WARC record #{record} is the last continuation of its series but has no WARC-Segment-Total-Length
warc/segmentation.total-length-not-last: WARC record #{record} has WARC-Segment-Total-Length but is not the last continuation of its series
warc/segmentation.total-length-mismatch: WARC record #{record}: WARC-Segment-Total-Length says {declared} bytes but the blocks of the series add up to {actual}
warc/segmentation.origin-not-found: WARC record #{record} (continuation) points to the origin {origin}, which is not in this WACZ
warc/segmentation.no-continuation: WARC record #{record} starts a segmented series, but none of its continuations is in this WACZ
warc/segmentation.extra-fields: WARC record #{record} (continuation) carries {fields} — segments after the first should carry only what continues the record
warc/payload-digest.desc: WARC records' WARC-Payload-Digest must match a fresh sha256 of the payload
warc/payload-digest.no-http-body: WARC record #{memberIdx} ({recordType}) has WARC-Payload-Digest but no parseable HTTP body
warc/payload-digest.non-sha256: WARC record #{memberIdx} uses non-sha256 digest "{algo}" — not verified
warc/recording-complete.desc: browserhive: surface how many recorded requests were incomplete/failed (WARC metadata records)
warc/recording-complete.incomplete: {incomplete} of {total} recorded requests are incomplete or failed ({percent}%)
warc/storage-store.desc: every WARC under archive/ must be stored with method STORE (0), not DEFLATE
warc/storage-store.zip-compressed: {entry} is zip-compressed (method {method}) — should be STORE (0) so CDXJ offsets seek correctly
